missions.title: First Strike

opponent.name: Warden Kessel
opponent.flavor: Digs in, waits, and expects you to bleed on her line.

intro: Two tanks, one soldier, and a scout report that says Warden Kessel left only a picket in the valley.
She is not wrong to be confident — she has held this ground for a year. She has simply never been rushed.
Select. Move. Strike. That is the whole of it today.

hints.text: Tap one of your tanks. Every tile it can reach this turn lights up.
Tap a highlighted tile to stage a move — tap it again to confirm.
Now tap the enemy to stage an attack. The tray shows the damage forecast before you commit.
Each unit gets one move and one action a day. When your second tank has swung too, end the turn.
Kessel's turn. Watch what she does with the forest — trees are armour out here.
Day two. Wounds don't heal on their own — finish the survivor and the valley is yours.

missions.title: Flag Country

opponent.name: Captain Vayle
opponent.flavor: Plays the percentages, never overreaches, never panics.

missions.objective: Take the three cities on the road, then capture Vayle's HQ.
intro: One road, three towns, and Captain Vayle coming down it from the north with a soldier and a scout car.
Ground you stand on is worth nothing. Ground you have raised a flag over pays you every single day.
Take the flags first. The HQ is only the last one on the list.

hints.text: Only infantry can capture. Select one of your three soldiers.
Roads are the cheapest ground to cross. Stage a move onto the nearest city and confirm.
Standing on a city isn't owning it. Choose Capture from the menu.
A capture takes two turns at full health, and stepping off resets it. Hold the tile.
Your tank cannot raise a flag — its job is to keep Vayle's scout car off the ones who can.
An HQ captures like any other tile. Walk a healthy soldier onto it and the war ends there.

missions.title: War Economy

opponent.name: Quartermaster Penn
opponent.flavor: Counts every coin twice, then spends all of them on you.

missions.objective: Out-build and out-earn Penn, then take his HQ.
intro: Three thousand in the war chest, one soldier on the field, and a factory that has been cold for a month.
Quartermaster Penn does not fight battles. He fights budgets, and he has never lost one.
Every property you hold pays a thousand a day. Spend it faster than he does.

hints.text: Tap your factory — the tile just above your HQ — to open the build menu.
Infantry cost 1000. Three of them take three cities; one tank you can't afford yet takes none.
A unit built today can't move today. Spend the rest of your funds, then end the turn.
Four neutral cities sit between you and Penn. Each one is 1000 a day, forever — go and take them.
Income compounds. Two cities ahead by day five is a tank ahead by day eight.
Funds sitting in the chest kill nobody. If you can afford a tank, build the tank.

missions.title: The High Ground

opponent.name: Red Rask
opponent.flavor: Charges first, reads the ground never.

missions.objective: Hold the pass and destroy Rask's armour.
intro: A wall of mountains with one road cut through it, and Red Rask on the far side with two tanks and no patience.
He has to come through a gap two tiles wide. You do not have to meet him in it.
Let the ridge do the work, and let the artillery do the arithmetic.

hints.text: Mountains stop tanks dead — only infantry can climb. Rask must use the road pass.
Terrain is armour. Forest and mountain soak damage; that bare road soaks none at all.
Artillery strikes two to three tiles away but cannot move and fire the same turn. Park it with the pass already in range.
Indirect fire never takes a counterattack. Shell them in the gap before they reach your line.
Hold the mouth of the pass with your tanks. A charge into the gap gives Rask the fight he wants.

missions.title: The Black Pines

opponent.name: Colonel Wren
opponent.flavor: Quiet, patient, and entirely comfortable in the dark.

missions.objective: Find Wren's column in the pines and take the HQ.
intro: The pines swallow everything: sightlines, scouts, and the last three patrols sent in after Colonel Wren.
You will see only what your own units can see. Everything else is a memory drawn on a map.
Send the recon ahead, take the crossroads city for the view, and don't walk into a treeline you haven't checked.

hints.text: Fog. You see only what your units see — the rest of the board is guesswork.
Your recon sees five tiles and moves eight. It's a torch, not a hammer — keep it ahead and keep it alive.
The city in the middle of the pines watches the whole crossing while you hold it. Take it.
Forest hides whatever stands in it until you're beside it. Treat every treeline as occupied.
Ghost markers show where you last saw something — not where it is now. Wren moves the moment you look away.
